findings.reason: Untrusted source: in tpacket_snd(), when the socket has po->has_vnet_hdr (PACKET_VNET_HDR sockopt), vnet_hdr = data (line 2672) points directly into the user mmap'd TPACKET TX ring frame (data comes from tpacket_parse_header() -> *data = frame + off, frame = packet_current_frame(po, &po->tx_ring, TP_STATUS_SEND_REQUEST)), which userspace can write concurrently; unlike the packet_snd() path that copies the header into a stack struct virtio_net_hdr via copy_from_iter_full, here the header is dereferenced in place with no READ_ONCE/private copy and no lock covering both accesses. Violated invariant: __packet_snd_vnet_parse(vnet_hdr, tp_len) at line 2676 validates csum_start+csum_offset+2 against hdr_len and hdr_len against tp_len, and tpacket_fill_skb() at line 2695 builds the skb (sock_alloc_send_skb sized from the shared hdr_len at 2680-2687; data copied into the skb), but the values actually consumed are re-fetched independently afterwards: virtio_net_hdr_to_skb(skb, vnet_hdr, vio_le()) at line 2719 re-reads hdr->csum_start/hdr->csum_offset from the same shared ring memory, and virtio_net_hdr_set_proto() at 2723 re-reads gso_type. A racing userspace writer can change csum_start/csum_offset (or flags to set VIRTIO_NET_HDR_F_NEEDS_CSUM) between the validation fetch and the use fetch. Unsafe use: the re-read unvalidated values flow into skb_partial_csum_set() via include/linux/virtio_net.h:54-59, which sets skb->csum_start/skb->csum_offset and ip_summed=CHECKSUM_PARTIAL on the TX skb; these become checksum indices consumed by checksum-offload computation (skb_checksum_help and driver TX csum paths read skb->data + skb->csum_start + skb->csum_offset). Counterevidence checked: skb_partial_csum_set (net/core/skbuff.c:4396-4411) does validate the SECOND fetch against skb_headlen(skb) in 32-bit arithmetic, so the 2719 re-read alone cannot push csum_start+csum_offset+2 past the skb's head length; the concrete hazard is the divergence window between the 2676 validation and the 2719/2723 uses (hdr_len/gso fields consumed at 2680-2681, 2863-2870-style sizing, and protocol selection at 2723), matching the seed's validate-once/use-a-different-fetch TOCTOU pattern on shared memory. Impact: validated-vs-used inconsistency on the mmap'd ring header; worst case OOB read/write during checksum computation in the TX path is bounded by the second (self-validating) fetch for csum fields, but gso_type/flags/hdr_len inconsistency between 2676 and 2719-2723 remains usable by an attacker. Note this pattern is upstream Linux behavior present in this snapshot; reported as a hypothesis per the seed mechanism, not as a proven exploit.

candidates.reason: virtio_net_hdr_to_skb(skb, vnet_hdr, vio_le()) re-reads the mmap'd TX ring vnet_hdr after __packet_snd_vnet_parse validated it at 2676 and tpacket_fill_skb consumed data at 2695; validated fetch and used fetch are independent reads of concurrently-writable user memory with no READ_ONCE/local copy.

virtio_net_hdr_to_skb reads hdr->csum_start/csum_offset once into locals start/off and passes them to skb_partial_csum_set, which checks (u32)start+off+2 <= skb_headlen(skb) with 32-bit arithmetic (no overflow) and sets skb->csum_start/csum_offset from the same local values; invariant holds whenever the caller's hdr is a private copy.

skb_partial_csum_set validates csum_start (headroom+start <= U16_MAX) and csum_end (start+off+2 <= skb_headlen) in u32 arithmetic before assigning skb->csum_start/csum_offset; checked value is the same used value, computed against the true linear length.

tun_get_user copies the vnet header into a stack struct virtio_net_hdr gso via copy_from_iter_full (line 1759); all later csum_start/csum_offset/hdr_len reads at 1762-1764, 1811-1814, and virtio_net_hdr_to_skb at 1855 use the private stack copy, so no shared-memory re-fetch exists.
tap_get_user copies vnet_hdr to the stack via copy_from_iter_full (line 647); the csum_start+csum_offset+2 check at 650-659 and virtio_net_hdr_to_skb at 709 both operate on the stack copy.
packet_snd() (sendmsg path) uses a stack struct virtio_net_hdr vnet_hdr filled by packet_snd_vnet_parse->copy_from_iter_full (2439); virtio_net_hdr_to_skb at 2916 consumes the private stack copy.

virtio_net_hdr_to_skb(skb, &hdr->hdr, ...) operates on the driver's own receive-path header (struct virtio_net_hdr_mrg_rxbuf in driver-managed memory built from virtqueue buffers), not on a concurrently-writable mmap'd user region; also an RX ingestion path rather than the untrusted TX csum_start/csum_offset ingestion this branch targets. Not fully traced to the DMA source, hence recorded rather than proven.

limitations: The reported tpacket_snd() finding's csum_start/csum_offset consequence is bounded: the second fetch at line 2719 goes through skb_partial_csum_set which independently re-validates against skb_headlen(skb), so the seed-style OOB during checksum computation requires divergence in hdr_len/gso/flags fields or their effect on skb sizing, not the csum pair alone; this weakens it to a validated-vs-used inconsistency hypothesis rather than a demonstrated memory-safety violation.
drivers/net/virtio_net.c:1024 header provenance (DMA-writable vs driver-private) was not fully traced; recorded as safe but unproven.

Other per-driver TX checksum-offload ingestion sites (e.g. drivers/net/ethernet/ibm/ibmveth.c:1297 skb_partial_csum_set) and vhost-net were not deeply audited; vhost-net does not assign skb->csum_start/csum_offset from guest memory directly in this tree (consumers go through tun/tap/virtio_net_hdr paths already classified).
No compile-time or dynamic reproducer was run; analysis is static line-level reading of the s02 snapshot.
